title: Egalitarian reservation, spill-forward recovery, and regional fallback for throttler outages
creator: Priya Nair
description: Context: Recent incidents showed our per-region admission controllers can enter soft outage modes (control plane lag, Redis throttles) leaving downstream customers with either total blackouts or first-come-first-served spikes that breach SLOs for priority tenants. Goal: design and ship a recovery mode that preserves proportional guarantees across customer tiers during transient limiter outages, gracefully sheds low-priority work, and allows regional failover without costly global coordination.
problem_statement: When a regional admission controller degrades we currently either fail closed (large customer impact) or fail open (unbounded spike + SLO violations). We need a deterministic, low-latency mechanism that: (1) preserves priority guarantees for reserved/paid customers, (2) spreads residual capacity fairly across tenants, (3) supports fast recovery and reconciliation once the controller returns, and (4) emits actionable telemetry for on-call.
proposal_summary: Introduce an "egalitarian reservation" layer: each tenant receives a small soft-reservation computed from long-term usage and committed capacity. During a local limiter outage we: (A) switch to soft-lease mode where reservations are honored up to a capped refill rate, (B) enable a spill-forward path where unused reservation credits can be forwarded to peer regions for short windows, and (C) apply a controlled shedding policy that degrades best-effort traffic first. The design uses lightweight vector clocks for lease versioning and deterministic token reconciliation to avoid oscillation.
acceptance_criteria: Reservations computed per-tenant and enforced during degraded mode with <= 10ms additional admission latency
Under simulated regional limiter outage, P0 tenants retain >= 95% of steady-state successful request rate while P2/P3 best-effort is degraded
Spill-forward mechanism transfers unused soft reservations to adjacent region within 500ms and reclaims credits deterministically on recovery
Reconciliation run clears 99.9% of transient credit drift without manual intervention
Observability: dashboards and alerts for reservation utilization, spill-forward transfers, reconciliation drift, and shed-rate visible in Console
Runbook for on-call with playbook steps and rollback instructions exists in Confluence
updates: 2026-02-12: Ticket created after postmortem for incident 2026-02-09. Initial problem framing and success criteria documented.

2026-02-19: Spike simulation completed — ran a 12-hour chaos test with 3 region leader restarts (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/TR/egalitarian-spike-sim). Observed baseline preservation for high-tier tenants but starvation for mid-tier in naive fail-open path.
2026-02-27: Design review with runtime team. Decided to use soft-lease with vector-clock reconciliation rather than a centralized broker to keep latency and availability targets.
2026-03-05: Implementation PR opened for admission adapter and credit ledger (github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4897). Unit tests and basic integration harness added.

2026-03-08: Load tests in our staging cluster with 1:10 P0:P3 mix showed spill-forward reduces cold-region drop rate by 68% compared to baseline. Noted edge-case where recovered region double-applies credits if reconciliation delayed.
2026-03-10: Mitigation for double-apply under review; proposed fix uses idempotent reconciliation tokens. Assigned to assignee for implementation before canary.
decisions: Avoid centralized quota broker to reduce single-point failure; favor local soft-lease with opportunistic peer transfers
Soft-reservations will be computed from a windowed 30-day usage percentile + committed capacity; algorithm documented in design doc
Spill-forward windows limited to 10s to bound resource exposure and simplify reconciliation
Circuit-breaker state transitions use three-tier timers: detection (100ms), enter degraded (200ms), full-fallback/blackout (5s) to avoid flapping
Telemetry will expose both per-tenant and aggregated reservation drift metrics to aid automated rollback thresholds
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger correctness and idempotent reconciliation; integration test against staging admission controllers with synthetic tenant traffic (P0/P1/P2/P3 mix); chaos runs with injected Redis latency and partial network partitions. Automated perf job to assert admission latency < 10ms added to CI.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged deploy to staging; 2) Canary in us-west-2 for low-traffic subset (5% traffic) for 48h; 3) Gradual ramp to 25% with continuous health checks; 4) If canary metrics meet acceptance ones for 72h, enable global rollout with 10% step increases and operator approval checkpoints. Rollback if reservation drift > 1% for P0 tenants or shed-rate > 5% for P1.
runbook_snippet: If region shows high reconciliation_drift_count: 1) pause spill-forward via ff flag; 2) trigger manual reconcile endpoint; 3) escalate to runtime on-call if drift persists > 10m; detailed steps in playbook link.
open_risks: Under extreme global overload spill-forward can propagate overload across regions — we mitigate by the 10s window and global emergency circuit-breaker
Accurate long-tail usage estimates required to avoid systematic under/over reservation; will roll out conservative estimates first
Reconciliation correctness must be bulletproof — any idempotency bug can cause double credit application; extra testing required
followups: ENG-700014 - formal verification of reconciliation idempotency
notes_for_PRD: This ticket is implementation-level work that implements behaviors described in PRD 'Regional SLO Failover and Load Shedding' (see product link). Close collaboration with PM (Diego Morales) and Design (Lin Zhao) required for UX of console panels and customer communication templates. Ensure legal is looped for any behavior that changes SLA guarantees.
communication_plan: Customer-facing postmortem template prepared; for Dedicated customers set expectation email before regional canary. Internal RFC circulated to SRE/Support/Account Management.
operational_cost_estimate: Estimated additional 2-3% CPU and 50MB memory per admission adapter instance for local ledger. Network overhead for spill-forward negligible at expected volumes.
implementation_notes: Ledger will be kept in memory with periodic durable checkpoint to Redis; checkpoint frequency tunable by deployment profile. Use incremental vector clocks to reconcile and avoid full state transfer.
qa_signoff: Pending - integration tests stable in staging as of 2026-03-09; final QA run scheduled before canary
release_notes_blurb: Adds a degraded-mode reservation and spill-forward recovery to protect high-tier tenants during local admission controller outages. Improves multi-region resilience and reduces customer-visible drops.
